purpose: OpenAI/Broadcom Jalapeño inference accelerator record with Hot Chips 2026 specifications and InferenceX results.

hardware.architecture_note: Purpose-built spatial LLM inference accelerator designed around locality, explicit placement of model state/KV cache, predictable synchronization, and a rack-scale connected domain.
hardware.networking_note: Hot Chips reporting describes a 128-accelerator local domain and a 2,048-accelerator global domain; the architecture is designed to keep model state local and reduce communication stalls.
hardware.availability_note: OpenAI plans to begin deployment inside its own compute infrastructure by the end of 2026. Gen 2 is in development and Gen 3 is taking shape; Jalapeño is not a retail product.
software_evidence: OpenAI reports that Codex with GPT-Astra helped bring GPT-OSS, DeepSeek R1, and Kimi K2.5 kernels to high performance; selected AI-generated attention/MoE blocks ran 1.5x-1.8x faster than prior expert-written implementations.

performance_evidence.summary: Across the three models, OpenAI reports 1.5x-1.9x more peak AI work per watt and 1.7x-3.6x lower end-to-end latency than the compared commercial GB200/GB300 systems.
performance_evidence.methodology_note: Results use single-token prediction and normalize using published package TDP; production systems may use different serving techniques such as multi-token prediction.

research_notes: 216 GiB HBM4, 15.4 TB/s memory bandwidth and 13.4 PFLOPS MXFP4 are Hot Chips 2026 presentation specifications reported by multiple technical outlets; OpenAI's benchmark page independently confirms the 700 W package rating and <=550 W sustained power in the tested workloads.

Do not treat the published InferenceX comparisons as a universal production-serving ranking: the comparison uses STP and package-TDP normalization, and serving stacks may use different speculative or multi-token techniques.
Jalapeño remains a datacenter infrastructure platform rather than a local/retail purchasing candidate.
